source: Sri Lanka Department of Agriculture, HORDI potato crop guide

entries.content: Potato prefers well-drained soil rich in organic matter with pH about 5.5 to 6.6; tuber initiation benefits from soil temperature below 24 C.
Tuber initiation and tuber bulking are particularly sensitive to inadequate water; use root-zone observations and calibrated moisture data to avoid both drying and waterlogging.
actions: Check moisture in the active root zone

entries.content: Potato tuber moth larvae may mine leaves or shoots and later tunnel into exposed tubers; tunnel entrances can contain dark waste material.
actions: Remove leftover tubers and crop residues

entries.content: Cutworm damage can include round holes on young leaves and plants cut near the soil surface, often with new damage appearing overnight.
actions: Inspect near damaged plants and soil surface

entries.content: Aphids commonly gather on tender shoots and lower leaf surfaces; heavy populations can curl young leaves, leave sticky honeydew, and transmit virus diseases.
actions: Use visual monitoring or yellow traps

entries.content: For bacterial-wilt risk, use clean seed tubers, improve field drainage, and avoid moving contaminated soil or equipment between fields.
actions: Clean soil from equipment before moving fields

entries.content: Regularly inspect potato crops for virus-like symptoms, manage insect vectors through integrated practices, and remove clearly affected plants using local extension guidance.
actions: Ask an agricultural officer before concluding a virus diagnosis
